name: Edged

profile.reading:
Edged Chicago ORD01 is a wholesale/colocation data center campus built and operated by Edged (Edged Energy) at 2835 Bilter Road in Aurora, Illinois, within DuPage County, one of several purpose-built campuses the company markets under its Edged brand across North America. According to the company's own published materials, the Chicago campus sits on more than 65 acres and comprises two connected buildings, ORD01-1 and ORD01-2: a two-story, 24-megawatt building and a larger single-story, 72-megawatt building the company says can be further subdivided for individual tenants, together totaling roughly 96 megawatts of critical IT load across the campus.

Edged designs its facilities to a Tier III, concurrently maintainable standard and advertises a 100% uptime service-level agreement, backed by an on-site electrical substation sized for the campus's full build-out, N+1 uninterruptible power supply and generator redundancy (with generators specified using Tier 4 Final emissions-compliant engines), and revenue-grade real-time power metering, infrastructure typical of large wholesale data center developments aimed at hyperscale and enterprise tenants rather than small retail colocation customers. Each building is described as having two loading-dock bays, around-the-clock access, and two meet-me rooms connecting to multiple carrier-neutral fiber providers through four physically diverse points of entry.

Cooling is a notable feature of the design: Edged uses a proprietary waterless, closed-loop system it calls ThermalWorks, built around glycol heat transfer with N+1 redundancy, which the company states achieves a Water Usage Effectiveness of 0.00 liters per kilowatt-hour, eliminating the evaporative water consumption typical of conventional data center cooling towers, a design choice with particular relevance in a region where large industrial water draws have drawn public scrutiny. The company also states the system supports liquid-cooled racks at densities above 400 kilowatts each, well beyond what traditional air-cooled data halls can accommodate, positioning the campus for high-density AI and HPC workloads alongside conventional enterprise IT.

Fire protection includes a double-interlock, pre-action water-mist system in the data halls with addressable, hot-aisle-focused smoke detection, and the campus is secured with perimeter fencing, biometric access control, and CCTV. Edged reports a projected mechanical PUE of 1.086 for the Chicago site and an estimated six-nines (99.9999%) availability figure. Individual tenants and per-building square footage have not been published by the company.

reading:
Edged is a data centre developer owned by Endeavour, a holding company founded by Jakob Carnemark, who previously founded Aligned. Its pitch is thermal rather than architectural. Edged buildings use waterless cooling supplied by its sister company ThermalWorks, marketed as supporting up to 70 kW per rack on air and up to 200 kW per rack with plug and play liquid cooling, and the company quotes a portfolio average power usage effectiveness of 1.15. Edged has announced or is developing sites in Atlanta, Dallas, Kansas City, Columbus and Phoenix in the United States along with Spain and Portugal, and publishes neither a corporate headquarters city nor a founding year.

The single row here is the Chicago campus, ORD01, at 2835 Bilter Road in Aurora, Illinois, on the DuPage County side of the city. The campus covers about 65 acres and is planned for three facilities. The first building, ORD01-1, is two storeys and roughly 210,000 square feet, and opened in February 2025 with 24 MW of IT load. The second, ORD01-2, is single storey, planned at 72 MW, and can be split into two facilities. The 96 MW figure that appears in the company's own launch announcement and throughout trade coverage is the campus total across all phases, not the load of the building that opened, and confusing the two is the most common error in listings for this site. ComEd is the serving utility. Edged projects the waterless design will avoid close to 380 million gallons of water a year once the whole campus is running.

Aurora is one of the more interesting municipal records in this registry, because the city rewrote its rules while Edged was already operating there. Data centres in Aurora had been permitted as warehouses. The city imposed a 180 day freeze on new applications from 25 September 2025 and adopted a new ordinance on 24 March 2026. It requires conditional use approval and City Council sign off rather than a by right warehouse permit, third party baseline sound studies and noise modelling, water and energy consumption reports, a cap on water use effectiveness of 0.2, a ban on evaporative cooling, and either on site renewable generation covering 25 percent of peak demand or storage able to supply 50 percent of peak demand for fifteen minutes, plus continuing public reporting of water use, energy use and noise. The city's own material counts ten data centres in Aurora, five operating and five in development, ranging from 9 to 98 MW, and notes that facilities can reach over 90 decibels without mitigation.

Edged worked with the city through that process and agreed to install electric vehicle chargers along Bilter Road. It is worth noting when reading the company's sustainability claims that a waterless, air and liquid cooled design is unusually well placed against rules written to restrict evaporative cooling, so the technology choice and the regulatory position reinforce each other.
